title: Thread Suspension / GC Pause Lease Violation
pattern: Assuming that checking lease validity is sufficient to authorize a subsequent action, ignoring potential thread pauses from garbage collection or VM suspension.
why_bad: Arbitrary pauses (up to minutes) can occur at *any* point in execution. If a pause occurs immediately after checking a lease, the lease may expire during the pause, but the thread will continue its unsafe action once resumed, leading to data corruption.
detection: Validating a lease or leader state in software and then performing an external side-effect (like database writes) without fencing tokens or database verification.
counterexample: Using fencing tokens (like generation counters) at the database layer to reject writes from stale leaders.
fix:
Utilize database-level fencing tokens to validate writes.
```sql
UPDATE database SET value = x WHERE leader_generation = current_generation;
```
